And you've advocated that international law needs changing in relation to the use of the media in the course of armed conflict. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact language I used, but yes, I -- yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You wrote: "The systematic breach of journalistic ethics in service of belligerent policy risking human rights abuse should also warrant intervention." Is that -- do you recall that or does that reflect your view?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you -- that remains your view?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Well, the word "intervention" means many things, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you are involved in some sort of promotion campaign for changing in international law to regulate what you regard as the abuse of the media?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any campaign of that kind. I've written on this. As you see, I've written elsewhere about it as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And in a nutshell, it may be it's not possible to do it in a nutshell, but is your suggestion that it should be made some sort of, broadly, war crime to abuse or misuse the media?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: No, I don't -- I mean -- no, I don't think I have a nutshell answer on that. My concern has been that the international community has in the conflicts of the 1990s been insufficiently sensitive to the role that media can play in an area of tension or an area of conflict and also insufficiently attentive to the constructive role that media can play in a post-conflict normalisation process. And that's what I've written about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thompson.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Krajisnik, you'd indicated that you'd have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you said you would have a few questions for Mr. Thompson. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I have had not an opportunity to read your report, however I see now that you dealt with a Serbian newspaper called Glas. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: My question to you is as follows: In the Serbian Glas did you ever come across my statements on ethnic cleansing? And let me remind you, on the 17th of October, 1992, and 21 December, 1992, there was a statement and an interview with Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I would need to check through the material to know if that was included here. So I don't -- I can't answer without doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: I have the newspaper here. I can provide it to you, if I'm allowed to do so by the Chamber. However, even if you don't remember maybe you can answer whether you have ever come across a statement of that kind anywhere. This is what I would like to hear from you.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Can you just clarify what you -- what -- just what kind of statement you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: On the 17th of October, 1992, and 21 December 1992 I said clearly that I was deeply opposed to any form of ethnic cleansing and forceful movement of population.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. The only -- I would refer you to footnote --

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could you please answer whether you read this or not. Have you read those statements of mine or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the witness was about to answer your question and he wanted to refer you to a footnote, a footnote you will not have seen. So therefore we'll invite the witness to explain what this footnote tells us. And then if he has done so, we can then see whether he has answered your question yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only -- thank you. The only material that I think of immediately as corresponding to that kind of statement is the sentence quoted in my addendum; it's footnoted with footnote number 10. And I don't know immediately if footnote 10 refers to that source. I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I do know, Mr. Krajisnik, is that 21st of December, 1992, interview in Glas Srpski is among the materials that has additionally been provided to the Chamber and is -- I don't know whether you received a copy or not --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that -- there's no need to ask the witness whether he has seen that because it's part of the material. It's now presented in the context of his testimony. And I saw that there are some statements there, just if I would correct then you would have said: "Personally, I'm against any kind of coercion and I strongly condemn every attempt to coerce people into moving out of their homes. That is why this term ethnic cleansing should be taken with a pinch of salt. It was used only in the report by Tadeusz Mazowiecki, Polish prime minister, in which he blamed everything on Serbs in former BiH in such a biased and hypocrite manner, giving the impression that it was commissioned." That's what it says. Is that what you wanted to draw the attention of the witness to?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is one of the reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the witness has seen it and it has been read to him. And the other one I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 17th October 1992 report is not in the materials that we submitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. If you'd like to read one or two lines or relevant lines to the witness, you may do so. Please read slowly, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: The interview was taken on 17th October. "Ethnic prisoners. 'I'm opposed to any form of ethnic cleansing.' This is what Mr. Momcilo Krajisnik said categorically. Every person who has to leave their home is a poor soul. We would oppose with all of our strength to every, even be it the smallest attempt to carry out ethnic cleansing. We will also oppose to the creation of ethnic prisoners and those were the Serbs in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, namely, in many towns, in many cities, in many settlements, especially in those where the SDA is in power. Serbs are imprisoned in various places and they are not allowed to move on -- move out. The story in Central Bosnia is somewhat different. The Croatian authorities allow every Serb to leave if they want to do so. Those who have decided to remain, nobody touches them. That is why we do not think that there has been any form of ethnic cleansing in Central Bosnia or, in other words, that the Serbs have been persecuted there. We will never forbid anybody to leave. Both Muslims and Croats can go if they wish to do so openly. And those national minorities in Republika Srpska who reside there, this is what I would like to tell them and emphasise: All the national minorities will be guaranteed all their human rights according to all the international conventions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put your question to the -- or was it just whether he had read this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Again, my question is as follows: Did the witness ever come across these two statements of mine?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: The OTP has said that this material was not presented -- was not given to me. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Krajisnik's question was: "Did the witness ever come across these two statements of mine," and it's already clear that the first article is in the materials submitted to the Chamber and has been reviewed by the witness. The second article, I believe, was not provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, while -- let's make -- try to make things a bit more simple. Mr. Krajisnik says: "That's what I said in an interview." Perhaps we could even invite the witness to see whether he could or could invite Mr. Krajisnik to present that interview. But being confronted now with this material, the first question is: Did you see it before? I take it the 21st of December is clear already. The other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't -- I don't know if at some point it was published since I have seen it. But I can say that to read such an opinion coming from Mr. Krajisnik is not a surprise to me. It's not news, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it change any of your opinions as you expressed in your report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid it wouldn't. While parts of that statement - only parts of it - are commendable, I don't believe that they went very far in reassuring the non-Serb population under Bosnian Serb control that they had any kind of future at all. On the contrary, I would have thought that the contrast between such commendable statements on the one hand and the events on the ground would have appeared grotesque to that population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: The question was whether you came across these statements during your research, not whether you received them from the OTP. Because these statements were given in 1992, not in 1995. And my second question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you're commenting on the answer of the witness. The witness has answered the question. Please put your next question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: In order for me to put the second question to you, I would like to lay the background to that question. Have you read the book the "Balkans Odyssey" by Mr. Owen? Does it say in the book that the parties to the conflict have engaged --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have put the question whether the witness has read the book. I haven't heard an answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness nodded his head and I took it as his answer. My mistake. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Did you read in this book which of the sides engage certain media to promote their war goals to serve as a propaganda machine for the promotion of their goals?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I read the book in early 1996 and I don't remember all of it. It's a long book. I do remember coming to the view that Lord Owen's opinions on the role of media in the war were problematic and not -- and simplistic, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: My question was clear, sir. I am going to rephrase it and put it to you again. If I put it to you that Mr. Owen claims that the Muslim and the Croat sides engaged the media, that they allocated funds for propaganda, would you agree with me or not? Would your opinion be different?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I simply don't remember that in Owen's book. I do remember a couple of brief statements about the role of media which -- which seemed -- I mean, I am trying to remember back nearly a decade, which said that -- basically a plague on all their houses, that the media everywhere were equally reprehensible. That I took to be Owen's view and it's a view which I don't have myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, before any further questions on this issue, we would request that the accused provide us with a page reference so we can check which page of the book he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know what page -- I take it that you are quoting from the B/C/S version, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us a clue as to, perhaps, chapter and it might be -- and the page number so the OTP would be in a position to verify the source.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll bring a copy of that page with me tomorrow. My question to the witness was whether he read that book. If he did, he should be able to remember. The page is not important in that, but tomorrow I will provide you with a copy of that in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the importance of pages is for the Chamber to decide on the request of the OTP, nothing more, nothing less, and that you bring the page number tomorrow and the page might not help out if the witness is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- today. Please put your next questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can provide the OTP with the page number reference, but it does not have to be admitted into evidence. I am not insisting on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I said you can put your next question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: My third question to you, sir. You were talking about threats and you mentioned threats to Mr. Karadzic. Do you remember the threats issued by Mr. Izetbegovic at the Assembly and in Kladusa and the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina and in Bosanska or rather Cazinska Kladusa. I can repeat the threat for you don't remember, to refresh your memory if you want me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see whether the witness can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember that Mr. Izetbegovic in February 1991 at the parliament said that he would sacrifice peace for a sovereign Bosnia and Herzegovina --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, this line is in evidence already many times. The Chamber is fully aware of what witnesses who do remember or who have any knowledge of it told us about it. There is no use in asking this witness who says that he doesn't remember them to read it to him unless the witness says: I -- it might well be, but I've forgotten exactly what it was. Under those circumstances, we could refresh his memory.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have heard Mr. Karadzic's statement. What I am trying to do is to refresh the witness's memory. He said that he never heard a single statement by the Muslim leaders. That's what I'm asking him whether he heard this particular statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In general terms, Mr. Krajisnik, it makes sense to refresh the memory of a witness if there are good grounds to believe that he has any personal knowledge but he might have forgotten specificities -- specific aspects of those events. Witness, did you ever concentrate on these kind -- since your report is very much focussing only on what side said, did you ever study, well, say fierce expressions by leaders of the other nationalities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I did my research, I was looking -- trying to look at what was happening to all the three peoples within Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And although not allowed, Mr. Krajisnik has expressed the line he would like you very much to remember. Does it ring any bell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This simple truth is that during my years of following very closely the events in Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would think it's extremely unlikely that I didn't come across that line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- reported somewhere or other. But do I now remember -- has he jogged my memory? No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Then, Mr. Krajisnik, this is a line which is in evidence many times. If there would be any specific question you would like -- on which you think the witness could add something to it by his own knowledge, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You lived in Zagreb. Did you hear the statement that Mr. Izetbegovic issued in Kladusa, which is actually close to Zagreb, that he would use arms to defend Bosnia --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I did not allow you to start with the next quote; I said: If you have any specific question on a quote. I did not allow you to read to the witness, but if you have any specific question, you could put that to the witness. Please be careful.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Did you hear Mr. Izetbegovic's statement, the one he gave in Kladusa?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: As with the other statement that you mentioned, I don't have it in my memory now. Did I come across it during ten years of daily involvement with these issue? I expect I did. But ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, I take it that there will be ample opportunity, if it ever comes to that, that you present this evidence during the presentation of the Defence case. This witness seems to not have any active knowledge on the matter. Please proceed to the next subject. That will be your last question. You said you had a couple questions, certainly not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: You were talking about the request to split Radio-Television Sarajevo in several parts, this was in 1991. Do you remember that? Do you know that at this moment in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and at the level of the Presidency there is a request to split the radio-television, and the request was put in by the Croatian side?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: And are you aware of the reasons put forth by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I think I know what they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you know?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Well, if I would be allowed just to point out that I don't see any connection now with the events of the early 1990s, but yes now the HDZ leadership now in Bosnia and Herzegovina today claims that it would be in line with its constitutional national rights to have a separate representation in federation broadcasting in the federation entity, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it confuses me a bit. In the question there was a split of Radio-Television Sarajevo mentioned in several parts. This was in 1991. And now you say: "I don't see any connection now with the events of the early 1990s," which is not fully understandable --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps if I can assist. The second part of the question from the accused was: "Did you know at this moment the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then I missed that. And please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was answering the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm talking about 2005 and I pointed out that I don't see any connection with 1991. But as far as 2005 is concerned, that is -- that is the situation. I hope very much that the HDZ leadership will not get its way because it would be very unfortunate for the future of public-service broadcasting in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: Just one more clarification with regard to this last question, and that will be my last question to you. Between 1990 and 2005, have there been -- has there been a constant request by the Croats to separate the broadcasting system and for them to have their own broadcasting channel? Has there been a -- has that been a constant request on their part?

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I don't know if it's been continuous. It's recurred, clearly. But this is in the -- the HDZ political pressure now for a separate channel is in the context of the Federation public service broadcaster, operating in the Federation entity. So it's post-Dayton. And this pressure has become stronger in proportion as the prospect of a functioning public-service broadcaster for the federation being realised, and the pressure is now all the stronger because from that leadership's point of view the danger -- the danger of a genuine Federation-entity broadcaster is greater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you said this was your last question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to thank you and I would also like to thank the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just have one issue which is a slight lack of clarity on page 5 of the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And it's under the heading of "control of RTVSA transmitters."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in your report at that part you said "between August 1991 and March of 1992 five of the 11 main transmitters belonging to the RTVSA were captured by Serb or Yugoslav army forces." You then list those five. Now, if you skip the next paragraph the first words of the following paragraph you say: "A few days after the capture of the Vlasic transmitter." Now, could you clarify the Vlasic transmitter was a sixth or was it one of the five --

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You've drawn attention to a bit of poor structure in my report. That was not one of the five, that was one of the further three which is mentioned on the tenth line down on the following page 6: "By the end of June 1992 three further transmitters had been seized by several Yugoslav forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have a relatively simple question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One of the documents that is presented to the Chamber is under number 5 on the list is a video of interview with Krajisnik. It bears as the date 1992/1993. It might be interesting for the Chamber to know when in 1992 or 1993 this was broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm not with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's under number 5.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Transcript of the interview with Krajisnik is --

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Uh-uh, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Production Serbian television channel S and then it says date 1992/1993. Whereas we have similar headings, for example, for the video interview of Krajisnik and Karadzic under 3 where it says, I think, January/March 1993, in the list it comes up with a rather specific date, which is the 15th of March, whereas in respect of this document --

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We only find 1992/1993.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: An answer to your question would not be difficult to obtain, but I'm afraid I don't have -- I don't have that historical detail in my head. It's -- it would be easy to obtain by finding out when the -- exactly when the events mentioned took place, the events mentioned in the first few paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARK THOMPSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry that I can't answer it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. You'll volunteer to check. In so far as our records have verifiable information, I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we do the following, I'm also looking at you, Mr. Stewart, it seems that the television programme gives quite some clues which could not leave such doubt. For example, on the second page I read: "Bosnian Serb Assembly ended last night in Zvornik," which means we have several events on the new Presidency to be formed I think and who that would be. Therefore, if the parties could agree on when that must have approximately been, that would be fine. If the parties are not in the position to do so, I'd like to ask the Prosecution to ask the witness then - if you could not agree - to see whether he has sources which would allow him to give further details. I'm also asking this specifically because in view of earlier questions on strategic goals, whether there were further supports or no, in this interview where Mr. Krajisnik says something about strategic goals and -- being realised or are realising as he says, in the interview at least. Then, Mr. Gaynor, could you give us a clue on why you make number 3 the 15th of March and whether there's any dispute? Because the document itself doesn't give a clue on that specific date. It says January /March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't enlighten you at this moment as to why that specific date appears there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please get that information at the earliest possibility. Then we have P855 where Mr. Krajisnik addresses a crowd in Foca or Srbinje. There's no date on that, neither on the original or on your list. Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Again, as Your Honour has probably noticed, there seem to be somewhat clues as to when it might be, but I will endeavour to find the best information as to the date of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you inform Mr. Stewart what you find and see if there's any dispute about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I will indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not suggesting that we ask the witness to wait and see what the parties can find, but just leave it for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand the procedure is that on all these date matters the Prosecution are going to just give us a quick --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Try to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- note on where they say they come from and see if we agree and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then inform the Chamber and if not, we might ask for a five-lines written report by this witness or by anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Sooner the better before we all forget what it was what we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We keep a nice list of pending issues. Did -- yes, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to be of assistance. If the Prosecution could give me a CD of all that and maybe I can help Mr. Stewart out and we can spot certain things because I don't really have the electronic form of either these talks or any other document. If you could give it to me today, it might be useful.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We've provided CDs with these videos to the Defence team. If the Defence team wishes to provide it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And here of course immediately security issues arise, et cetera, et cetera. If -- your assistance is greatly appreciated, Mr. Krajisnik. If counsel could resolve the matter, then I think they're at least grateful for you having offered to assist them. Is there any issue triggered by the -- well, I wouldn't say questions by the Bench, but at least by the issues raised by the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Not on our side, Your Honour. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nodding no for the Defence. Nodding no for the Prosecution as well, Mr. Gaynor. Then I'd like to thank you, Mr. Thompson, for coming to The Hague to answer the questions mainly of the parties, not many of the Bench, but -- and I'd like to wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Mr. Thompson out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if this is a correct time to raise this. I want to correct very quickly a point made by Mr. Hannis on Monday on the record in relation to some information which Your Honours requested. The information provided by Mr. Hannis was incorrect. I'd like to correct the record on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the information?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The first one was KRAJ 606. Your Honours requested clarification as to whether the parties were referring to two statements dated 13 October 2001 or if not two, which one. And I can clarify that the Prosecution has agreed to withdraw both statements dated the 13th of October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has agreed with itself or with the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, we inform the Chamber that we withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's withdrawn. So at least you apply for withdrawal of these statements which you presented to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. The second point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is in relation to witness Samardzic, who is KRAJ 515. Your Honours gave us the opportunity to explain further the relevance of that material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We appreciate the opportunity to explain further the relevance and we shall not be providing any further explanation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware -- first of all, I think this information reached the Chamber already. And you may be aware if the Chamber asks for the relevance and you say you have got nothing further to say for the relevance that you take the risk that the Chamber considers it to be irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. And if I can just provide one further clarification. In Mr. Hannis's submission the issue with relation to KRAJ 606 was mixed up with relation to the other witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's always good to know the backgrounds of errors, but we accept that they are made now and then. I would first of all like to thank the interpreters and technicians for again allowing us to continue, even if not specifically asked for to continue for ten minutes. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00. Mr. Registrar, that would be Courtroom III again -- yes, it's Courtroom III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 1st day of July, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
